_note: Column divider positions for Repertoire tables, as fractions of the CROPPED table width (apply docs/repertoire_crop_bounds.json first). Derived 2026-09-08 by taking the median of pipeline/row_detect._detect_vertical_dividers across every page of a group -- steadier than one visual reading, and within a group the positions vary by only 1-2% of width against columns 17-25% wide. Spread seasons (1890-91..1897-98) are keyed by season, put the DATE column at the table's RIGHT edge, and have 5 theaters. Single-page seasons (1898-99 onward) are keyed 'season:parity' because the recto/verso gutter offset shifts the table within a season crop (splitting by parity drops sigma from 0.056 to ~0.020); they put the DATE column at the LEFT and have 3 theaters. Groups are gated on even spacing, since theaters are equal-width -- check 'evenly_spaced' and 'source' before trusting one. NOTE on the final divider of spread seasons: it bounds the DATE column, which is NARROWER than a theater, so extrapolating it by one theater width overshoots. 1890-91 (0.966) and 1891-92 (0.982) overshot into the date column itself and were corrected against the page to 0.900 and 0.945; the rest landed in a consistent 0.918-0.943 band. Spread seasons therefore fail the even-spacing check by design. IMPORTANT: these fractions are relative to the CROPPED width, so any change to docs/repertoire_crop_bounds.json invalidates them and they must be rescaled or re-derived. 1891-92, 1898-99 and 1902-03 were rescaled on 2026-09-08 for exactly this reason.
